title: Prompting
lede: How you ask decides what you get back. A few questions on context, structure, examples and knowing when the model is guessing.
description: How you ask decides what you get. Test your grip on context, structure, examples and knowing when the model is guessing.

questions.q: You ask AI to rewrite a report and the result is bland and generic. What usually fixes it fastest?
options: Ask again and add the word 'better'
Give it the audience, the purpose and an example of the tone you want
Switch to a bigger model
Break the report into smaller pieces
questions.why: Generic output almost always means missing context. Audience, purpose and a sample of the voice you want give the model something to aim at.

questions.q: Which is the strongest signal that a model is guessing rather than knowing?
options: The answer is long
It uses confident language with specific-sounding but unverifiable details
It asks you a clarifying question
It formats the answer as a list
questions.why: Confidence isn't a reliability signal. Precise details you can't trace back to a source are the thing to check.

questions.q: You need output in a fixed structure every single time. What works best?
options: Ask politely
Describe the structure and show one filled-in example
Repeat the instruction three times
Write the instruction in capitals
questions.why: One worked example does more than any amount of description. Show the shape you want rather than explaining it.

questions.q: You're drafting an email to a client and want AI to match your usual voice. What's the most reliable approach?
options: Tell it to 'sound professional'
Paste two or three emails you've actually sent and ask it to match that style
Use a longer system prompt with adjectives like 'warm' and 'concise'
Ask for three versions and pick the best
questions.why: Real samples beat adjectives. The model can mirror patterns it sees — vague labels leave too much room to guess.

questions.q: A model gives you a statistic you plan to use in a presentation. What should you do before citing it?
options: Trust it if it sounds reasonable
Verify it against a primary source or ask the model where it came from
Rephrase it so it sounds less definitive
Switch models and see if they agree
questions.why: Models can invent plausible numbers. Always trace claims back to something you can point to in the room.
